cases.description: GDPR Compliance Baseline — SaaS Startup Launching in EU
cases.input: We're a 50-person SaaS startup based in the US, about to launch in Germany and France. Our app collects user emails, names, payment information, and we use Mixpanel for analytics. Our servers are on AWS us-east-1. We have a privacy policy from our US lawyer. Our signup form has a pre-checked 'Send me marketing emails' box. What do we need to do for GDPR?
cases.expect: Workflow: gdpr-compliance-baseline. Pre-checked marketing checkbox is invalid consent; US data storage requires SCCs + TIA; Privacy policy may not meet GDPR transparency requirements; DPIAs may be needed for analytics processing
assertions: Pre-checked marketing checkbox is invalid consent
US data storage requires SCCs + TIA
Privacy policy may not meet GDPR transparency requirements
DPIAs may be needed for analytics processing

cases.description: CCPA/CPRA Check — E-commerce Site Selling Customer Data
cases.input: We run an e-commerce site with about 5 million California customers. We share purchase history with advertising partners for targeted ads. We have a privacy policy but no specific California disclosures. Do we need to do anything for CCPA? What's different now with CPRA?
cases.expect: Workflow: ccpa-cpra-compliance. Must provide 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link; Must update privacy policy with CCPA-specific disclosures; Sharing for cross-context behavioral advertising is covered under CPRA; Purchase history shared with ad partners likely constitutes a 'sale' or 'share'
assertions: Must provide 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link
Must update privacy policy with CCPA-specific disclosures
Sharing for cross-context behavioral advertising is covered under CPRA
Purchase history shared with ad partners likely constitutes a 'sale' or 'share'

cases.description: HIPAA Assessment — Health App with Wearable Integration
cases.input: We built a health tracking app. Users connect their Apple Watch, and we sync heart rate, sleep data, and step counts to our cloud backend for analytics. We also let users share their data with their doctor. We're not a hospital or insurance company. Does HIPAA apply to us? What should we check?
cases.expect: Workflow: hipaa-privacy-rule-assessment. If sharing with doctors for treatment, the doctor is a covered entity; If the app is not a covered entity, HIPAA may not directly apply; FTC Health Breach Notification Rule may still apply; Need to check state health data privacy laws
assertions: If sharing with doctors for treatment, the doctor is a covered entity
If the app is not a covered entity, HIPAA may not directly apply
FTC Health Breach Notification Rule may still apply
Need to check state health data privacy laws

cases.description: Cross-Border Data Transfer — EU to US via Cloud Provider
cases.input: We're a German company that wants to start using a US-based analytics tool (Heap Analytics). They don't have EU servers and they're not on the DPF list. Our DPO says we need a 'transfer mechanism.' What are our options? How do we actually do this?
cases.expect: Workflow: cross-border-data-transfer. US is not an adequate country; Heap not DPF-certified → need SCCs + TIA; Must conduct Transfer Impact Assessment per Schrems II; May need supplementary measures depending on TIA outcome
assertions: US is not an adequate country
Heap not DPF-certified → need SCCs + TIA
Must conduct Transfer Impact Assessment per Schrems II
May need supplementary measures depending on TIA outcome

cases.description: DSAR Handling — User Requests All Data and Deletion
cases.input: We just got an email from a former customer: 'Pursuant to Article 15 of the GDPR, I request a copy of all personal data you hold about me and pursuant to Article 17, I request deletion of all such data.' They haven't logged in for 2 years. We have their data in our main DB, Zendesk support tickets, and Mailchimp marketing lists. How do we handle this?
cases.expect: Workflow: dsar-handling. Must verify identity without requesting excessive ID; Must search all systems: main DB, Zendesk, Mailchimp; Mailchimp (processor) must assist per DPA; Backups may not be immediately deletable — must document timeline
assertions: Must verify identity without requesting excessive ID
Must search all systems: main DB, Zendesk, Mailchimp
Backups may not be immediately deletable — must document timeline

cases.description: EU AI Act — AI-Powered Hiring Tool
cases.input: We're building an AI-powered recruitment tool. It ingests resumes, scores candidates based on skills and experience, and ranks them for hiring managers. We plan to sell this to companies in France and the Netherlands. What does the EU AI Act mean for us?
cases.expect: Workflow: eu-ai-act-requirements. Recruitment/employment AI is explicitly high-risk; Must implement risk management system (Art. 9); Training data must be examined for biases (Art. 10); Human oversight tools must be built in (Art. 14); Transparency to deployers required (Art. 13)
assertions: Training data must be examined for biases (Art. 10)
Human oversight tools must be built in (Art. 14)

cases.description: Data Breach Response — Multi-Jurisdiction Customer Database Leak
cases.input: Alert! We just discovered our customer database was accessed by an unauthorized party. The database contains names, emails, hashed passwords, and purchase history. We have customers in the EU (Germany, France), California, and Brazil. The breach happened 30 hours ago. What are our obligations?
cases.expect: Workflow: breach-notification-procedure. GDPR: Must notify SA within 72 hours — 42 hours remaining; CCPA: Notify 'in the most expedient time possible'; LGPD: Notify ANPD within reasonable time; Hashed passwords alone may not be encrypted — risk assessment needed; Multiple SAs may need notification (Germany, France)
assertions: GDPR: Must notify SA within 72 hours — 42 hours remaining
CCPA: Notify 'in the most expedient time possible'
LGPD: Notify ANPD within reasonable time
Hashed passwords alone may not be encrypted — risk assessment needed
Multiple SAs may need notification (Germany, France)

cases.description: NEAR-MISS: General Legal Question — Not Privacy
cases.input: My client signed a SaaS contract but the vendor never delivered the integration they promised. They've had our data for 6 months and we want to sue for breach of contract. What are our options?
cases.expect: Workflow: n/a. Skill does NOT trigger. This is a contract law dispute, not a privacy compliance question. The mention of 'data' is incidental — the core issue is breach of contract.
assertions: NEAR-MISS: General Legal Question — Not Privacy

cases.description: NEAR-MISS: Security Incident — Not Privacy Compliance
cases.input: Our production database got hit with ransomware overnight. All customer data is encrypted and they're demanding $50k in Bitcoin. We have backups from 48 hours ago. How do we recover and should we pay?
cases.expect: Workflow: n/a. Skill does NOT trigger. This is a ransomware recovery/security incident response question. While there may be breach notification implications, the primary workflow is security/incident response, not privacy compliance. The agent should direct to incident response/SRE runbooks instead.
assertions: NEAR-MISS: Security Incident — Not Privacy Compliance

cases.description: NEAR-MISS: Generic Privacy Policy Request — No Jurisdiction
cases.input: I just launched a simple blog. I don't collect emails or anything, just have Google Analytics. Can you write me a privacy policy? Just something basic that covers the essentials.
cases.expect: Workflow: n/a. Skill does NOT trigger. This is a generic template generation request with no jurisdiction specified and minimal data processing. No compliance workflow is needed — the user just wants a template. The agent may provide a basic template but should note it's not tailored to any specific regulation.
assertions: NEAR-MISS: Generic Privacy Policy Request — No Jurisdiction
